name: Electrical & Electronics
summary: The Gen 6 Camaro factory electrical system is a GM network architecture (BCM, IPC, GMLAN CAN) with the AGM battery in the trunk, an E92 ECM running the direct-injected LT1/LT4, and underhood/rear fuse-relay blocks. The race build strips the body electronics and replaces them with a purpose-built system: trunk battery with FIA-style master cutoff (mechanical 4-post switch or Cartek solid-state isolator), a programmable PDM instead of fuses/relays, a Chevrolet Performance E92 controller kit or a GDI-capable standalone ECU, a CAN-networked dash/logger, keypad and chassis sensors, and a mil-spec Tefzel/DR-25 harness with Deutsch bulkhead connectors.
overview:
Architecture. Power flows battery (trunk, right side) → master cutoff → main 1/0 cable through the cabin along the passenger sill → firewall power junction → starter, and from the junction (fused) → PDM. The PDM switches and protects every load (ECU, ignition, fuel pumps, fan, intercooler pump, lights, comms) and reports currents over CAN. Grounds return through a dedicated battery-negative cable, two engine-to-chassis straps and a star ground for the electronics. The ECU, PDM, dash/logger, keypad, GPS/IMU, lambda controller, tire-temp sensors and (if used) the race ABS share one or two 1 Mbit/s CAN buses.

Factory vs race. The Gen 6's body modules (BCM, IPC, SDM, radio) are VIN-linked on the GM network and are not needed to run the engine when a Chevrolet Performance LT1/LT4 controller kit is used (the kit supplies a programmed E92, engine harness with fuse box, DBW pedal, O2/MAF, oil and fuel-pressure sensors and the fuel pump power module). Note GM's warning that pre-2022 LT controllers must not be used on 2022+ LT crate engines, and that early (4-pin) and late (3-pin) LT4 fuel-rail pressure sensors need matching kits. The direct-injection LT limits standalone choices to GDI-capable systems (Holley Terminator X Max Gen V LT DI kits 550-1623/550-1624, MoTeC M1 GPR-DI on M122/M142/M182 class ECUs) unless the race engine is converted to port injection (then MoTeC M150, Holley Dominator, Haltech Nexus etc. apply). Keeping OE electric power steering and OE ABS/StabiliTrak requires keeping their network messages alive – decide this with the steering and brakes systems before designing the harness.

Rules. SCCA GCR wording (quoted secondhand) requires a master switch in either battery cable that cuts all electrical circuits except an on-board fire system, accessible from outside – on closed cars in front of the windshield on the cowl/fender (driver side) or below the center of the rear window – marked with the spark/blue-triangle decal. NASA CCR wording (quoted secondhand) allows radio, fire system and life-support devices to remain live. Whether a solid-state isolator is accepted varies by series and inspector – confirm before buying. Rain lights: many series require one; FIA standard 8874-2019 covers homologated rain lights (Lifeline 421-100-011, Cartek CK-LRS-15RM/16CM). Transponder: MyLaps direct-power, ≤ 60 cm above ground with clear view of the track, on a 2.5 A fused switched supply. Always read the current rulebook for your class.

Common failure points. Loose or under-sized main cables (hot restart failures), chafed harness at the firewall/seat/cage crossings, engine-ground straps loosening, connectors not latched, fan and fuel-pump channels tripping on inrush, alternator run-on after the master is switched off (needs field kill / dump resistor), CAN termination errors, and DI injector wiring noise corrupting crank/cam signals.
buildNotes: Phase 1 (bare shell): decide battery, master switch, PDM/ECU and bulkhead locations; weld ground studs and battery box mounts; cut and doubler-plate firewall and rear bulkhead connector holes; install rivnuts for every harness P-clamp along the planned routes; then paint.
Write the electrical load list and channel map (current, PWM, logic) before buying a PDM – fans, fuel pumps, starter and ignition set the channel sizes and the alternator size.
Choose ECU strategy (Chevrolet Performance E92 controller kit vs GDI standalone) and whether OE EPS/ABS are retained before building the harness – it drives CAN design.
Build the cabin electronics panel (PDM, ECU, star ground, fuses) and the dash harness on the bench; build the engine harness on a board measured from the installed engine.
Run the main 1/0 battery cable inside the shell along the passenger sill before seats and interior go in; crimp lugs with a hydraulic crimper and adhesive heat shrink.
Install engine ground straps with the engine (phase 6); install starter, alternator, and their cables before headers if access is tight.

Power-up sequence: continuity test every circuit → check for shorts to ground → first power with ECU/ PDM disconnected → PDM config → ECU power and comms → sensor plausibility → crank with no fuel to verify sync → fuel pressure → first fire.
Verify CAN termination (~60 Ω), ground offsets (< 50 mV ECU-to-battery), master switch kill with engine running, and cranking voltage drop (< 0.5 V positive path) before shakedown.
Install rules items last but test them at the first tech: external kill, decals, rain light, brake lights, transponder.

schematics.title: Power distribution: battery → master cutoff → PDM channels → loads
schematics.description: Main power path from the trunk battery through the master cutoff (mechanical switch or solid-state isolator with engine-kill signal), main cable to the firewall junction, starter branch (unfused) and fused PDM branch, PDM output channels to every load, and the auxiliary always-hot block for circuits rules allow to stay powered.

schematics.title: Charging & starting circuit
schematics.description: Cranking current path (battery → master → main cable → junction → starter → engine block → ground straps → chassis → battery negative), and the charging path (alternator B+ → junction → main cable → battery) with ECU/PDM control of the alternator L-terminal and starter solenoid.

edges.label: aux pole: alt run-down on OFF

schematics.title: CAN bus / network topology
schematics.description: Two CAN buses at 1 Mbit/s: Bus 1 (engine/power) ECU – PDM – dash – keypad – lambda; Bus 2 (chassis/data) dash – GPS/IMU – I/O expanders – IR tire sensors – brake temp – ABS (Bosch M5 CAN or OE ABS via gateway) – camera. 120 Ω terminations at each physical end. Factory GMLAN (500 kbit/s) only if OE EPS/ABS retained.

schematics.title: Sensor & data-acquisition block diagram
schematics.description: Every sensor channel and which device acquires it: ECU (engine control sensors), front/rear I/O expanders (chassis analogue), CAN smart sensors (IR, GPS/IMU), all logged by the dash/logger and overlaid on video.

nodes.label: Engine sensors: crank, cam, knock, MAP/TMAP, ECT, fuel-rail P, TPS

schematics.title: Grounding scheme
schematics.description: High-current returns via the unibody (engine straps → front stud → body → rear stud → battery negative), plus a separate star ground in the cabin for electronics and sensor 0 V references returned only to their own device.
